runs.text: Cuſtume do reino, ou nação, cida-

lines.note: Fǔzocu is fūzoku, the customs of a country or community. The scan clearly has u with caron, not the OCR's second F, and nação rather than noção.
de completes cidade from the preceding physical row. Cities join kingdoms and nations as communities whose customs are being defined; no new entry begins here.
Fuzonbun denotes an ill-considered opinion or imprudence. The negative fu and zonbun, a judgment or view, fit both the Japanese formation and Portuguese explanation.
The adjective fuzonbunna qualifies mono, a person. The Portuguese equivalent begins Peſ- here and continues with soa on the next physical line.
soa completes the word for person, followed by imprudente. This short continuation belongs to the same example and should not be mistaken for a separate headword.

runs.text: Paa comprida calçada de ferro de que

lines.note: Fuzuqi names a long iron-shod digging implement. Paa is the printed Portuguese spelling for a spade; it is not replaced by modern pá.

runs.text: vſão os lauradores, ou os que fazem vallos.

lines.note: The implement is used by farmers and people making ditches. vallos is an older Portuguese form; its doubled l is retained rather than modernized.
The regional label X. precedes the contrast with Cami, where Suqi is said. X. and the embedded Japanese name Suqi are upright here; the surrounding explanation is italic.
Fuzzucuri has the printed inflection u, utta and the sense of inventing or devising. Its historical consonant pattern is not regularized to a modern spelling.
The second sense concerns cutting and trimming paper. Camiuo fuz continues across the physical break without supplying an unprinted hyphen.

The continuation forms fuzzucuru, with qiriſoroyuru as an alternative, cutting evenly. Enlargement shows an irregular oblique ink trace above the second o, not a secure tilde or length mark; the unaccented OCR reading is retained with this uncertainty recorded.
The third sense is planning or preparing something quietly. caladamẽte is the printed nasal abbreviation, not a reason to expand the diplomatic text.
The noun Fuzzucuri is an arrangement or invention. It closes the F material before the separate heading announcing words beginning with G.

The large decorated G combines with the small A to form GA, read ga (ガ), not the OCR's Bzmo A. The opening introduces the particle's nominative use. The automatic hint currently omits the separately styled G; the overlapping crop includes the whole initial.
natiuo completes Nominatiuo. The dictionary qualifies this use as speaking humbly; humilmente is the actual Portuguese spelling and should not gain an extra b.
Fitoga maitta means that a person came. Fito, not Bito, and maitta, not maicta, are supported by both the scan and the Japanese construction; Vt is the italic example marker.
The Portuguese completes 'a person came'; Soregaxi begins the next example. It is the first-person expression soregashi, not another Portuguese word.
ga mairǒzuru completes 'I shall go.' The historical future form in -ǒzuru is intelligible without replacing it by a modern conjugation.
A new Item gives ga a genitive function. The split ge/nitiuo is physical line wrapping; the decorated initial beside this row is not additional text.
Soregaxiga mo begins soregashi ga mono, my thing. The noun is divided across lines without a visible hyphen; this spacing is preserved.
node gozaru completes the possessive example, translated as a thing of mine. The slightly worn o in gozaru remains supported by the syntax.

runs.text: Pospoſta esta particula aos verbos ſignifica às

lines.note: The dictionary next describes ga after verbs as a connective. Its Latin-derived terminology is historical explanation, not an instruction to rewrite the Japanese examples.
mas and porem give the adversative sense 'but.' Vomeni starts the respectful expression o-me ni, whose verb follows on the next row.
cacarǒtote maittaga means coming intending to meet someone, followed by an intervening obstacle. ſaxiuǒ is the historical obstacle expression; its unusual form is retained.

runs.text: &c. Vim para vos ver, porem ſo-

lines.note: go/zatte completes the polite existential verb. The Portuguese says 'I came to see you, but'; the &c. is explanatory typography, not Japanese reading material.
breuindo completes sobreuindo, an affair having intervened. The next Item opens another grammatical function rather than another lexical headword.
Cǔtaga yoi is glossed as it being good to have eaten. This is the contracted past of eating, not a word that should be changed to modern kutta.

runs.text: bom ter comido. ¶ Item, De accuſatiuo.

lines.note: The explanation closes the eating example and labels the next use accusative. This is the dictionary's grammatical classification, retained without imposing modern terminology.
Feiqeno yuraiga qiqitai means wishing to hear the origins of the Heike. The ga-marked object explains the preceding accusative label.

runs.text: ouuir o principio das couſas do Feique. Tẽ ou

lines.note: The Portuguese paraphrases hearing the beginnings of the Heike affairs. Feique is printed italic within the explanation; the embedded Japanese name remains available for typeface review.

runs.text: tros modos de falar menos principais os quaes

lines.note: tros completes outros from the previous row. The dictionary notes other, less central usages of ga; this is continuous Portuguese prose.
na arte refers the reader to a grammar for those additional uses. No title beyond the printed word arte is supplied in the transcription.
This Ga is now a lexical noun, pride, spirit, or one's own opinion. The scan supports opinião with its missing i restored, not OCR's opinão.
Gauo voru is ga wo oru, breaking or bending one's pride. The printed uo and vo conventions make the Japanese expression intelligible without modernizing it.
The same expression is introduced again in a metaphorical use. per met. is explanatory Portuguese/Latin abbreviation and remains italic.

runs.text: eſpantarſe, ou ficar frio de ver algũa couſa

lines.note: The figurative sense is being startled or chilled by seeing something unusual. The adjective naming the unusual thing continues on the following line.
Gauo fucai and tçuyoi fito describe a deeply or strongly self-willed person. The conspicuous uo is retained even where modern idiom might suggest a different particle.
The gloss describes someone with strong spirit and pride. Ga at the end starts another example, not an isolated Portuguese word.

runs.text: Ter teſo em ſua opinião, ou

lines.note: uo tatçuru is ga wo tatsuru, maintaining one's position. The Portuguese has opinião; its i is not the OCR's j.
Gauo daſu is showing one's spirit or resolve. The scan reads plain u, and Mostrar has no extra h; the explanation continues at the top of column two.
This is the completion of Gauo daſu from column one: spirit or resolve to do something. Its initial position does not make it a separate entry.
Ga is glossed pato, a duck. This Sino-Japanese bird term is separate from the grammatical particle and the preceding noun for pride.
Gabi is explained through caico and mayu, silkworm and cocoon. The following figurative sense concerns eyebrows; the small mark near mayu is not securely an accent and is not expanded.

runs.text: Permet. Roſto bem parecido de molher que

lines.note: Permet. introduces the metaphorical sense: an attractive woman's face. The reference is to the silkworm-like eyebrows described next, not a correction to the preceding literal definition.

runs.text: tem as ſobrancelhas como o bicho quando faz

lines.note: The woman's eyebrows resemble the worm when it makes silk. This explains the conventional moth-eyebrow image while preserving the dictionary's own zoological wording.
aſeda completes the description of silk production. The article and noun appear joined here; they are not silently separated for modern Portuguese readability.

runs.text: Aduerb. Modo de ſoar a agoa

lines.note: Gabugabu is an adverbial representation of the sound of water. The following line specifies drinking; Aduerb. belongs to the italic explanatory text.
Gabugabuto nomu means drinking with a gulping sound. The Japanese sound word and quotative to align directly with the Portuguese setting.
The gloss is drinking with that noise. eſtrondo supplies the sound-image, not a different action or another Japanese lemma.
Gabumeqi describes a vessel rocking strongly. Fune is the embedded Japanese word for boat within the Portuguese explanation; its typeface can be reviewed independently.
Gabun is one's own view, vaga zonbun. The small i is the explanatory marker, not a syllable of the following Japanese phrase.
Gabunuo tatçuru means standing by one's judgment. Ter begins the Portuguese idiom ter mão, whose completion is on the next row.

runs.text: mão em ſeu parecer, & juizo. ¶ Item,

lines.note: mão em seu parecer expresses maintaining one's opinion or judgment. The next Item extends the noun beyond this immediate example.
The additional sense is possession or capacity. The scan reads Poße, not Poßte; the OCR inserted a t into the double-s ligature.
Gabutçucaxi is the causative rocking verb, with ſu and aita inflections. The object, the boat, occupies the following short row.
a Fune supplies that boat object. Its being Japanese within Portuguese does not alone justify changing the scanned typeface.
Gabutçuqi is cross-referenced to Gabumequ with Idem, quod. The headword ending uita is retained as historical notation rather than rewritten as modern -ita.
mequ completes Gabu-mequ, the verb of rocking. This short row is genuine body text, not a catchword.
Gabugabuto ſuru has the same rocking sense in this location. It should not be conflated with the earlier drinking expression in -nomu.
Gacai describes the appearance or scale of works and buildings. The following example illustrates a substantial construction.
Vôqina gacai is a large-scale work. The printed pilcrow omitted by OCR is restored; the circumflex reading in Vôqina is retained from the scan.
bra completes obra, followed by houses as examples. This is the completion of the construction gloss, not the start of another G-entry.
Gaccai is extensive or profound learning, literally learned attainment. The unhyphenated profun/da division is kept as printed rather than repaired editorially.
da ſciencia closes that definition. The S. label stays italic under the established convention; no expansion is inserted into the text.
Gaccǒ is a place of study such as a university. The Portuguese is eſtudos, not eſtados, which is a clear meaning-changing OCR error.
Gachi is the suffix meaning generally or frequently. The initial is G, not C; both the following examples and the visible form support the correction.

runs.text: Vſaſe ſempre depois de outros nomes. Vt,

lines.note: The dictionary says this form follows other nouns. Its wording is preserved even if modern grammatical descriptions would classify some bases differently.
Vazzuraigachini gozaru means being frequently ill. The historical spelling corresponds to wazurai-gachi, not an unrelated word containing z or q.
Yudangachina mono is a person prone to carelessness. The preceding mente completes frequentemente across the physical row break.
The Portuguese explicitly describes habitual carelessness, then Tori- opens a third example. The printed double-s ligature in Peßoa is retained.
Torigachini ſuru means taking a disproportionately large share. The Portuguese spacing in a ventajadamẽte is retained even though the expression is semantically continuous.
The share exceeds what others receive of something. This completes the comparative explanation of the previous example.
Gacu, Manabu is learning or study. The example repeats Gacu ſuru; the OCR's Gucu conflicts with the scan and the immediately preceding headword.
Estudar is the one-word Portuguese gloss 'to study.' The short row remains associated with the Gacu ſuru example.
This Gacu has the hill sense, explained by Voca, oka. The semantic distinction from learning is explicit; the S. remains part of the italic explanation.
The music sense has Gacuuo ſôſuru, performing music. Tã- begins tanger; OCR's Tz- has mistaken a nasalized a for z.
ger completes tanger, playing musical instruments, with deſcantar as an alternative. The text does not require a modernized musical terminology.

runs.text: Titolo eſcrito em taboa, ou rotolo.

lines.note: Gacu here denotes a title written on a board or scroll. Titolo and rotolo are retained historical Portuguese spellings.
Gacuuo vtçu is attaching that written title or tablet. The visible pilcrow before the example is restored; vtçu is Japanese utsu, not an English abbreviation.

runs.text: titulo, ou rotolo em algũa parte.

lines.note: The title or scroll is affixed somewhere. This prose closes the example before the next compound begins.
Gacudǒ is manabu michi, the way of learning. The Portuguese describes arts or sciences; the caron-bearing o is kept as printed.
encias completes ciencias across the line break. It is not a separate lexical item and should stay in the same explanatory sequence.
Gacufen is the border of a hill, vocano fotori. Its f corresponds to historical h in hotori, and the gloss independently confirms that reading.
ou morro closes the alternative Portuguese hill term. The S. is a usage label rather than a Japanese syllable.

The lexical identification is gakugei, learning and arts, but the print appears to begin Cacuguei. NINJAL gives Gacuguei; that lexical authority alone does not justify overriding the visible C. Sciencias and artes replace clear OCR corruptions.
Gacuguiǒ is learning and practice, manabi voconǒ. The b of manabi is worn but supported by the Japanese pairing and the definition.
virtudes, ou penitencias expands the practical or religious aspect of learning and practice. The Gacu- below is a catchword, separate from this body row.
